current_status.before: Rescinded by court order as of 2026-09-23. Imperial County Superior Court Judge Jeffrey B. Jones entered judgment 2026-09-04 in favor of developer Imperial Valley Computer Manufacturing, LLC, finding neither Ordinance 1616 (the original moratorium) nor Ordinance 1618 (its ~10-month-15-day extension) made the causal finding of a 'current and immediate threat to public health, safety, or welfare' required by Gov. Code section 65858. A peremptory writ of mandate issued 2026-09-11 directs the County and Board of Supervisors to set aside both ordinances and stop using them to withhold, suspend, or refuse data-center permits. The County has said (per KYMA, 2026-09-22) it is working on a new moratorium addressing the court's concerns; no replacement had been adopted as of 2026-09-23. The Data Center Advisory Committee, created alongside the moratorium, continues to meet (inaugural meeting 2026-09-17) and is unaffected by the ruling. Separately, a different judge (L. Brooks Anderholt) has ordered a full CEQA environmental review of the underlying data center project in a related case, so the project itself remains stalled notwithstanding the moratorium's invalidation.
current_status.after: Ordinances 1616 and 1618 were repealed and set aside by the Board on October 6, 2026 in compliance with the court writ; the county said the urgency repeal took effect immediately. A separate October 6 moratorium was reported in local news; its later status was not verified.

outcome.before: Moratorium (Ordinances 1616 and 1618) adopted and extended to run through mid-2027, then invalidated by the Imperial County Superior Court (Judge Jeffrey B. Jones) in Imperial Valley Computer Manufacturing, LLC v. County of Imperial: judgment entered 2026-09-04, peremptory writ of mandate issued 2026-09-11 ordering the County to set aside and cease enforcing both ordinances because their findings did not satisfy Gov. Code section 65858's 'current and immediate threat' standard. The County has 30 days after service of the writ to file a return; county officials say they are preparing a new moratorium that addresses the court's findings. The Data Center Advisory Committee process continues separately.
outcome.after: The Board repealed and set aside Ordinances 1616 and 1618 on October 6, 2026, in compliance with the Superior Court writ. A separate 45-day moratorium was reported adopted that day; its later status is unresolved.

On 2026-09-01 the Fiscal Court reconsidered and unanimously adopted substantive revisions to the draft regulations (still numbered KOC 26-920-5): striking all references to 'large'/'hyperscale' data centers while adding a 10 MW maximum power-capacity cap (effectively banning hyperscale projects), raising the square-footage cap for 'medium' data centers to 110,000 sq ft, and requiring two weeks' advance notice to property owners within 1,000 ft of a proposed site's neighborhood meeting. County Attorney D. Berry Baxter, backed by outside zoning counsel and the Kentucky Association of Counties, concluded KRS 100.211(8)'s 90-day deadline for zoning MAP amendments does not apply to this zoning TEXT amendment, so no statutory deadline forces a vote. The Fiscal Court's public hearing and final (second-reading) vote on KOC 26-920-5 is now calendared for 2026-10-06, after this research date. The moratorium (KOC 25-910-508, extended by KOC 25-910-520 'until data center regulations are approved') has no fixed end date -- it remains the operative instrument until that vote occurs (or another statutory event ends it), consistent with an Aug. 19, 2026 news report confirming the moratorium 'remains in place' pending the Fiscal Court's next action.

Amends SMC 23.84A.008 to define "data center" as a facility used primarily for storing and processing digital data, with power capacity over 20 Megavolt-Amperes and requiring uninterruptible power, and imposes a moratorium on the filing, acceptance, processing, or approval of applications to establish or expand such uses.

Section 2 exempts expansions of no more than an additional 20 MVA at facilities operating on the effective date that meet the definition or would meet it except for existing capacity at or below 20 MVA. Section 6 adopts Attachment A work plan under RCW 36.70A.390.

key_provisions.after: CPUC must require electrical corporations to file data center transmission, distribution and generation tariffs; generation tariffs include cost-recovery mechanisms of at least 10 years. Community choice aggregators and electric service providers must adopt generation tariffs by 2028-01-01.

key_provisions.after: Requires data center water-use estimates to water suppliers and local governments for initial licenses or permits and annual use reporting on renewals; includes data center demand in urban water suppliers’ shortage assessments.

key_provisions.after: Directs CPUC to assess opportunities for rate structures addressing data center transmission and distribution costs, load and procurement costs, and residential cost pressures.

key_provisions.before: Requires CPUC report to the Legislature by 2027-01-01 on whether new data center loads shift electrical costs to other customers; repeals 2031-01-01.
key_provisions.after: Authorizes CPUC to assess whether new data center loads shift electrical corporation costs to other customers; requires submission and public posting of an assessment completed under the section by 2027-01-01. Section 913.22 is repealed 2031-01-01.

key_provisions.before: California Technology Innovation and Ratepayer Protection Act; would require CPUC tariff for participating data center customers, cost responsibility for transmission upgrades, early termination fees, clean-energy procurement, demand response participation, and no cost shifting to nonparticipating customers.
key_provisions.after: Requires CPUC by 2028-01-01 to establish or update tariffs and electric rules for participating customers, including protections against cost shifts and a transmission-level interconnection tariff with cost responsibility and early termination terms. Section 945.3 applies to data centers entering new transmission-level retail service interconnection agreements on or after 2027-01-01; demand response participation is optional.

key_provisions.before: Would bar CEQA categorical exemptions for data center projects and allow qualifying data centers to seek environmental leadership development project streamlining if they meet conditions for energy, water, infrastructure costs, labor, and community benefits.
key_provisions.after: Removes categorical CEQA exemptions for data center development and operation, with specified facility exclusions; adds qualifying data center and geothermal powerplant projects to environmental leadership development project eligibility, subject to statutory conditions. This combines environmental review requirements with conditional judicial streamlining.

key_provisions.before: Defines a large energy use facility as a NAICS 518210 facility using or able to use 20 MW or more. Requires regulated utilities to create a separate rate class and tariff that assigns or allocates costs to those facilities and mitigates cost-shifting and grid-reliability risks.

Requires utility rate classifications and service/security agreements to allocate costs and protect reliability. The 180-day rate-filing deadline runs from finalization of Commission regulations, not enactment.

key_provisions.before: Creates a compensation framework for property owners within 1,000 feet of a data center for value loss, business revenue loss, or adverse impacts such as noise, vibration, traffic, stormwater burden, or lighting; limits concurrent home-rule powers.

key_provisions.before: Directs the Center for Local Government Services to provide data center ordinance assistance and model municipal standards.
key_provisions.after: House-amended PN 3174 proposes that the Local Government Commission develop and publish a model data-center zoning ordinance and provide municipal technical assistance, stakeholder consultation, annual updates and public comment. The print replaces the Center for Local Government Services as the responsible body; this is a proposal, not an enacted statewide zoning mandate.

key_provisions.before: Amends Right-to-Know Law to prohibit nondisclosure agreements concerning data center construction, development, or location.
key_provisions.after: House-amended PN 3724 proposes computer-data-center incentive certification and retention conditions: a community-protection plan, project-footprint reporting and specified NDA certification. The plan and NDA conditions exclude centers below 10 MW peak demand. Separate exceptions concern specified pre-construction engagement requirements where construction began earlier, and NDA certification for previously certified owners/operators or qualified tenants. This is not a general amendment banning every data-center NDA under the Right-to-Know Law.

key_provisions.before: Amends the Municipalities Planning Code to allow a municipality to impose a 180-day pause on considering new data center development applications while it establishes or revises zoning ordinances for such facilities; applications filed during the pause are deemed received once the pause ends. Appears to be the bill introduced from the 'Proposed Zoning Consideration Period' co-sponsorship memo (#48467).
key_provisions.after: Senate-amended PN 3727 would let a municipality adopt a public-meeting resolution pausing acceptance of new data-center land-development applications for up to 180 days, retroactive to specified public notice. Earlier applications are exempt and continue under the applicable earlier rules; submissions during a pause are deemed received the following day after it ends. Repeat use is barred for 18 months following formal expiration or repeal. This is optional local authority, not a statewide pause.

key_provisions.before: Amends the Municipalities Planning Code to give a municipality the option to impose a temporary (reported as up to 18 months per news coverage) moratorium on accepting/considering new applications for high-impact data centers while it revises ordinances and develops conditional-use standards.
key_provisions.after: Pre-introduction memo proposing municipal authority to consider a temporary data-center moratorium; its official page links to SB 1345. The separately retained bill row pa-sb1345 describes the later PN 1889 resolution, maximum term and exceptions. This precursor is not an additional independent bill or an adopted municipal pause.

The official page links to SB 1359, separately retained as pa-sb1359. This precursor proposal is not an additional independent bill or enacted statewide moratorium.

key_provisions.before: Amends the Municipalities Planning Code to let a municipality impose a 180-day pause on considering data center development applications while it establishes/revises zoning ordinances for such facilities; applications submitted during the pause are automatically deemed received once the pause expires.
key_provisions.after: Pre-introduction memo proposing time for municipalities to develop data-center zoning rules; its official page links to HB 2496. The associated bill, separately retained as pa-hb2496, now contains the PN 3727 optional new-application pause with duration, earlier-application and repeat-use limits. status.after: Legacy precursor memo linked by the official memo page to HB 2496. The associated bill passed the House on 2026-06-24 and was reported amended with first consideration in the Senate on 2026-06-30. These are the bill's procedural events, not a second passage of the memo.

key_provisions.before: Amends the Municipalities Planning Code to give municipalities the option to impose a temporary moratorium (reported as up to 18 months) on accepting/considering new applications for high-impact data centers while revising ordinances and developing conditional-use standards. Bill page's own 'Memo Subject' field reads 'Empowering Municipalities to Place a Moratorium on Data Center Development,' closely matching the 'Proposed municipal moratorium' co-sponsorship memo (#48540).
key_provisions.after: Re-reported PN 1889 proposes optional municipal resolutions temporarily pausing acceptance and consideration of specified new high-impact-data-center applications for up to 18 months, retroactive to the required public notice. It requires planning findings and hearing notice, preserves listed unrelated/maintenance activities, and exempts previously approved matters and qualifying pre-existing power-generation-site agreements. It does not itself enact a statewide or local moratorium.

key_provisions.before: Prohibits certain nondisclosure agreements between public agencies and data centers, a Senate companion in subject matter to House HB2359 (Right-to-Know Law NDA prohibition).
key_provisions.after: Re-reported PN 2007 proposes a Data Center Transparency Act covering defined predominantly server-use facilities with peak electric demand of at least 10 MW. It combines specified public-agency NDA limits, at least two local public meetings and utility-application documentation before approval, restrictions on defined foreign-entity-controlled facilities, and energy/water-report certifications. Its proposed chapters have separate 180-day, immediate and 60-day commencement clauses; none supplies an enacted date here.

end_condition.before: Until PUCT and ERCOT complete the comprehensive verification and audit; projects that fail applicable requirements must be denied grid connection.
end_condition.after: Comprehensive verification and audit is required before additional interconnection approvals; the separate denial requirement applies to noncompliant projects. The letter states no fixed end date. Satisfaction of the prerequisite through 2026-11-05 is unverified.

key_provisions.before: Directs PUCT and ERCOT to verify and audit every data center advancing through ERCOT interconnection before it may move forward, pausing the Batch Zero process pending the required review.
key_provisions.after: Directs PUCT and ERCOT to conduct a comprehensive verification and audit of all data centers advancing through ERCOT interconnection before additional data centers are approved to move forward; noncompliant projects must be denied connection. Required information includes public financial assistance, power, water and cooling, community impacts, and ownership.

status.before: Governor directive issued 2026-08-03; ERCOT implementation notice issued 2026-08-03.
status.after: Governor directive signed 2026-08-03. Current legal effect and satisfaction of its audit prerequisite through 2026-11-05 are unresolved.

key_provisions.before: Requires PUCT/ERCOT large-load planning and interconnection standards; applies to large loads at a default 75 MW single-site threshold; addresses interconnection studies, cost allocation, co-location, and emergency curtailment
key_provisions.after: Directs PUCT standards for new or expanded ERCOT interconnections exceeding a single-site demand threshold of 75 MW unless PUCT determines a lower threshold necessary. Other provisions have distinct scopes: Section 39.170(b) uses at least 75 MW, while Section 39.170(a) applies to certain transmission-voltage loads interconnected after 2025-12-31. Also addresses studies, cost recovery, financial commitments, qualifying co-location and conditional curtailment.

key_provisions.before: Adds Va. Code section 15.2-2209.4. Requires localities to obtain a sound-profile site assessment for new high energy use facilities of 100 MW or more near homes or schools within 500 feet; allows optional review of water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forestland.
key_provisions.after: Published chapter/code site-assessment framework requires an applicant's sound assessment before specified local approvals for a new facility reasonably anticipated to require at least 100 MW of retail utility power. Sound impacts concern homes and schools within 500 feet of the facility property boundary; other resource assessments are optional, and utility substation/voltage information is also required subject to stated qualifications. The framework preserves the existing-approval/expansion exception; its phrase “does not exceed an additional 100 megawatts or more” is not converted into a definitive boundary here. The chapter labels the provision 15.2-2209.4; the observed code publishes it as 15.2-2209.5. Later force is not independently confirmed.

key_provisions.before: Would require State Corporation Commission certificates of operation for new high-load facilities exceeding 25 MW, including review of grid sufficiency and customer cross-subsidy risks.
key_provisions.after: Would require State Corporation Commission certificates of operation for new high-load facilities exceeding 25 MW, including review of grid sufficiency and customer cross-subsidy risks. The introduced eligibility condition concerns facilities not operating before 2026-07-01; that proposed applicability date is not an enacted effective date.

key_provisions.before: Requires registered water users that provide offsite water to report potable and reclaimed water volumes supplied to data centers with DEQ air permits, along with other use categories where available.
key_provisions.after: Published water-reporting act requires covered registered offsite suppliers to report potable and reclaimed water separately for qualifying air-permitted data centers. Other use categories are required to the extent available without utility billing-system modifications; quarterly volumes may substitute where monthly data are unavailable. The act expressly becomes effective 2027-01-01; enactment does not establish that it was already operative at the observation date.

key_provisions.before: Would prevent utility costs substantially related to serving data center customers of 100 MW or more from being recovered from non-data-center customers unless rates substantially recover those costs from data centers.
key_provisions.after: Would prevent utility costs substantially related to serving data center customers of 100 MW or more from being recovered from non-data-center customers unless rates substantially recover those costs from data centers. The introduced cost condition also requires that the relevant costs would not have been incurred but for that data-center demand.

key_provisions.after: Introduced proposal addressing specified localities' data-center zoning, including industrial designation, residential impacts and mitigation measures; incorporated into HB 153. Incorporation does not establish enactment of every introduced HB 511 provision.
